title: Vision Plans Enrollment Rule: One Open Enrollment per Covered Person
content:
**Enrollment and Eligibility Manual — Vision Plans**

**Rule.** A subscriber may hold one vision enrollment for each person covered under the subscriber's coverage tier, so there is no fixed cap per subscriber. A person may not have a second applied or active Cascade vision enrollment while one is applied or active. The persons enrolled must fit the coverage tier in the same way as for dental PPO coverage tiers: member only, member and spouse, member and children, and family.

**What decides it.** Whether a person already has an open enrollment is decided from the enrollment records, not from what the caller says. A new vision enrollment is matched to existing ones by the covered person's name together with their date of birth. Only an existing enrollment of that person that stands applied or active blocks the new one. An enrollment that stands terminated or cancelled does not.

| Existing Cascade vision enrollment of the same person (same name and date of birth) | May a new vision enrollment be opened for that person? |
|---|---|
| None | Yes |
| One that stands applied | No |
| One that stands active | No |
| Only enrollments that stand terminated or cancelled | Yes |

**Counting per subscriber.** The limit is per person, not per subscriber. A subscriber on a family coverage tier may therefore hold as many vision enrollments as there are persons covered under that tier, one each.

*Example (hypothetical household).* A subscriber covers a spouse and two children under a family tier and opens four vision enrollments, one per person. A fifth enrollment for one of the children, while that child's first enrollment is active, is not opened, because the child already has an active Cascade vision enrollment.
